Subject: Performance SLO follow-up: context window / max tokens impact (FinCo)

Thanks again for taking the call today — good to meet you both. Quick recap and next steps from our end on the performance/SLO topics we discussed (latency targets, throughput, concurrency, streaming requirements) with a focus on context-window and max-token impacts. Attaching a short SLA note and our recent KV-cache latency CSV for reference.

Recap (what we heard):
- Target user experience: interactive chat for customer support flows (streaming start-of-response important).
- Scale: ~200 concurrent active sessions during peak; average 8-10 RPS aggregated across endpoints.
- Typical prompt sizes: 4k input tokens historic average, but some workflows will require up to 28-32k context windows (full transcript history) + up to 2k output tokens.
- Desired SLOs: start-of-stream (first token streamed) ideally <300ms p95; end-to-end full-response completion p95 <= 2.5s for median prompts, with allowances for larger context windows.

Preliminary notes on context window impact (high level):
- Context size increases KV-cache memory and attention work. For decoder-only architectures we typically see sub-linear token decode cost increases, but attention over long context grows roughly O(N) per decode step in our serving stack for cross-attention-like components (practical impact depends on kernel-level optimizations and kv-cache locality).
- For a 32k input context vs 8k, we observe roughly 1.5-1.9x increase in end-to-end latency under equivalent hardware/config, all else equal (model, batch size, quantization).
- Streaming mitigations: we can deliver first tokens quickly by prioritizing prefix attention kernel paths and warm KV-cache; full completion still scales with output length + context overhead.

Questions / asks from us to make the perf run effective:
1) Can you share a representative set of prompts (anonymized) covering the 4k typical and the 28-32k worst-case flows?
2) Expected concurrency distribution (spiky vs flat) — are the 200 concurrent users sustained or short bursts?
3) Any hard constraints from compliance/procurement on test environments (e.g., must use Private deployment or can we run on Dedicated hosted capacity)?

Proposed next steps:
- We’ll run a targeted perf run using your anonymized prompts on a mirrored workload (recommended: dedicated pool + streaming enabled) — aim to show first-token latency, sustained throughput, and p95 completion time across 8k vs 32k contexts.
- Tentative window: Wed Apr 28 or Thu Apr 29 for the perf run. Please confirm availability.
- I’ve attached a one-page mutual action plan and our perf-SLA note for review.

Attachments: redwood-performance-sla.pdf, kv-latency-tests.csv, mutual-action-plan.xlsx

Thanks — I’ll coordinate the perf run once you share the prompts.

Great questions — see a concise breakdown below. I’ve kept numbers conservative and noted the hardware assumptions and config knobs you asked about. We can provide a short procurement-friendly bullet list as well; pasted that at the end.

Short latency table (estimated, per-request full-response completion p50 / p95) — typical config: streaming enabled, dedicated pool, continuous KV-cache, small batching (preferred for start latency):
- 7B (quantized q4): 8k context, output 512 tokens -> p50 ~400ms / p95 ~950ms. 32k context -> p50 ~650ms / p95 ~1.5s.
- 13B (quantized q4/q6 hybrid): 8k context, output 512 tokens -> p50 ~300ms / p95 ~700ms. 32k context -> p50 ~500ms / p95 ~1.2s.
- 70B (float16 / sparsely quantized): 8k context, output 512 tokens -> p50 ~650ms / p95 ~1.6s. 32k context -> p50 ~1.0s / p95 ~2.5s.

Per-token decode latency (ballpark) on A100/H100 class GPUs:
- 7B q4: 6-10ms/token (H100 faster), 13B q4: 8-15ms/token, 70B fp16: 18-35ms/token. These are approximate and vary with optimized kernels and sequence position.

Notes and mitigations:
- First-token / streaming: to hit <300ms p95 for first token we recommend: (a) small or no micro-batching for initial request routing, (b) warm KV-cache for session histories you expect to reuse, and (c) prioritized scheduling for low-latency routes.
- Batching tradeoffs: larger batching increases throughput efficiency (tokens/sec) but also adds queueing latency for first-token. For interactive flows we tune for small batches (N<=4) and rely on kernel-level throughput to keep costs reasonable.
- Context-window impact: moving from 8k -> 32k typically increases memory pressure and causes ~1.5-1.9x end-to-end latency as noted earlier. Quantized models help control memory but don’t remove attention compute growth.
- KV-caching: yes — session-level KV caching is viable and recommended. It reduces repeated attention over shared prefixes and improves p95 for repeated-turn conversations. For very large unique contexts (always new 28-32k inputs), caching benefit is smaller.

Deployment / hardware assumptions:
- Baseline numbers above assume dedicated A100/H100 class GPUs with Redwood production kernel set and aggressive kernel selection (we’ll share exact instance SKUs in the procurement note).
- If you plan to use our Private deployment on your cloud, we can produce equivalent numbers for your target instance types during the perf run.

Procurement-friendly bullets you can drop into an internal note:
- Recommended configuration: Dedicated pool, streaming enabled, session-level KV cache, quantized 13B for best latency/cost balance for FinCo workloads.
- Expected p95 full-response completion for typical prompts (8k context, 512 output): ~700ms or lower on A100/H100 for 13B q4 hybrid.
- Expect 1.5-1.9x latency increase for 32k vs 8k contexts; plan for dedicated capacity if 32k flows are frequent.

Next steps:
1) We’ll stand up the perf run using your anonymized prompts — we recommend the 13B quantized profile for the run unless you want a cross-model comparison.
2) Proposed perf run dates: Wed Apr 28 (preferred) or Thu Apr 29. We’ll need approx 90 minutes of test window.
3) If these numbers look reasonable, we’ll share a short addendum to the mutual action plan with recommended capacity and a draft SLA line item.

I’ve attached an updated perf note and the kv-latency CSV (already in the thread). If you want exact instance SKUs and our raw microbenchmark logs we can include them in the perf run deliverable.
